description: Broad outlook. Inferences flagged; fiction excluded as belief evidence.

evidence_levels.documented: stated in a cited source (Verne's reported words, firsthand observation, or reliable reference)
evidence_levels.inferred: reasoned from multiple sources; see reasoning
evidence_levels.speculative: plausible but weakly or not supported by collected sources

records.claim: Stated aim: to depict the whole earth and the universe while achieving beauty of style.

citations.quote: My object has been to depict the earth, and not the earth alone, but the universe

records.claim: Felt fortunate to live in an age of discoveries and inventions.

citations.quote: born in an age of remarkable discoveries

records.claim: Contemporaries saw him as the storyteller of a practical, scientific century (Claretie); Verne himself equated machines with art (locomotive vs Raphael).

citations.quote: as much pleasure in watching a steam-engine or a fine locomotive at work as I have in contemplating a picture by Raphael
Nous en sommes aux contes scientifiques

records.claim: Devoted to the sea; imagined nothing more ideal than a sailor's life.

citations.quote: I can imagine nothing more ideal than a sailor's life

records.claim: Saw his family as happy and deliberately unambitious ('none of us have been ambitious').
records.caveats: Sits awkwardly with his own expressed craving for recognition.

citations.quote: none of us have been ambitious

records.claim: Later work and remarks have been read as increasingly pessimistic about science and the future; the EB notes 'very gloomy predictions as to the future of the novel'.
records.reasoning: EB's remark is secondary; pessimism in late novels is a reading of fiction (what he wrote), not proof of belief. Needs letters of 1890s-1905.

citations.quote: very gloomy predictions as to the future of the novel

records.claim: Valued all learning as eventually useful ('Nothing that one has learned is ever wasted').

citations.quote: Nothing that one has learned is ever wasted
